preamble: In Avestan, the Proto-Iranian glottal fricative *h (itself from Indo-Iranian *s) was replaced by a velar nasal written ⟨ŋ⟩ before r, so that Iranian *-hr- appears as Avestan -ŋr-. Comparison with Sanskrit, which keeps the original *s, shows the development clearly. The phonetic value of the Avestan nasal signs is debated (some scholars read the related sign ⟨ŋh⟩ as a nasalized [h̃]), but before r the spelling shows a plain nasal in place of h. No parallel case is known outside Avestan.
phoneticEffects: Nasalization, Change in Place of Articulation, Change in Manner of Articulation

examples.note: Proto-Iranian *-hr- (< Indo-Iranian *-sr-) appears as -ŋr-; other Iranian languages keep h or lose it (Middle Persian hazār).
Same -sr- > Iranian *-hr- > Avestan -ŋr- development; Wiktionary gives the Sanskrit and Avestan forms as cognates.
